queries.title: Popular non-explicit tracks since 1990
queries.sql:
SELECT name, popularity, release_date, TO_CHAR((duration_ms || ' milliseconds')::interval, 'MI:SS') as duration
FROM tracks
WHERE popularity > 70
  AND release_date >= DATE '1990-01-01'
  AND NOT explicit
ORDER BY popularity DESC, name
LIMIT 50;

queries.title: Pattern matching and IN
queries.sql:
SELECT name, release_date, tempo, valence
FROM tracks
WHERE name ILIKE '%love%'
  AND time_signature IN (3, 4)
  AND valence > 0.8
ORDER BY tempo DESC
LIMIT 30;

queries.title: How much of a date do we actually know?
queries.sql:
-- release_date is padded to the 1st when the source only knew the
-- month or the year. This column says which.
SELECT release_date_precision, count(*) AS tracks
FROM tracks
GROUP BY release_date_precision
ORDER BY tracks DESC;

queries.title: Every decade at a glance
queries.sql:
SELECT (EXTRACT(YEAR FROM release_date)::int / 10) * 10 AS decade,
       count(*)                                   AS tracks,
       round(avg(popularity), 1)                   AS avg_popularity,
       round(avg(duration_ms) / 60000.0, 2)        AS avg_minutes,
       round(avg(energy)::numeric, 3)              AS avg_energy
FROM tracks
GROUP BY decade
HAVING count(*) > 100
ORDER BY decade;

queries.title: FILTER, and why it beats CASE
queries.sql:
SELECT (EXTRACT(YEAR FROM release_date)::int / 10) * 10 AS decade,
       count(*)                          AS tracks,
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE explicit)  AS explicit_tracks,
       round(100.0 * count(*) FILTER (WHERE explicit) / count(*), 1) AS pct_explicit
FROM tracks
GROUP BY decade
ORDER BY decade;

queries.title: Percentiles, not just averages
queries.sql:
SELECT round(avg(duration_ms) / 1000.0)  AS mean_seconds,
       percentile_cont(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY duration_ms) / 1000.0 AS median_seconds,
       percentile_cont(0.95) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY duration_ms) / 1000.0 AS p95_seconds,
       max(duration_ms) / 1000.0 AS longest_seconds
FROM tracks;

queries.title: Top 3 tracks per decade
queries.sql:
WITH ranked AS (
  SELECT name,
         popularity,
         (EXTRACT(YEAR FROM release_date)::int / 10) * 10 AS decade,
         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
           PARTITION BY (EXTRACT(YEAR FROM release_date)::int / 10) * 10
           ORDER BY popularity DESC, name
         ) AS rnk
  FROM tracks
)
SELECT decade, rnk, name, popularity
FROM ranked
WHERE rnk <= 3
ORDER BY decade, rnk;

queries.title: Year-over-year change with LAG
queries.sql:
WITH yearly AS (
  SELECT EXTRACT(YEAR FROM release_date)::int  AS year,
         round(avg(energy)::numeric, 3)        AS avg_energy
  FROM tracks
  GROUP BY year
)
SELECT year,
       avg_energy,
       LAG(avg_energy) OVER (ORDER BY year)              AS prev_year,
       avg_energy - LAG(avg_energy) OVER (ORDER BY year) AS change
FROM yearly
WHERE year BETWEEN 1960 AND 2020
ORDER BY year;

queries.title: Rolling 5-year average (frame clause)
queries.sql:
WITH yearly AS (
  SELECT EXTRACT(YEAR FROM release_date)::int AS year,
         round(avg(danceability)::numeric, 3) AS danceability
  FROM tracks
  GROUP BY year
)
SELECT year,
       danceability,
       round(avg(danceability) OVER (
         ORDER BY year ROWS BETWEEN 4 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW
       ), 3) AS rolling_5yr
FROM yearly
WHERE year >= 1950
ORDER BY year;

queries.title: RANK vs DENSE_RANK vs ROW_NUMBER
queries.sql:
SELECT name,
       popularity,
       ROW_NUMBER() OVER w AS row_number,
       RANK()       OVER w AS rank,
       DENSE_RANK() OVER w AS dense_rank
FROM tracks
WHERE release_date >= DATE '2015-01-01'
WINDOW w AS (ORDER BY popularity DESC)
LIMIT 25;

queries.title: Artists with a consistently strong catalogue
queries.sql:
WITH artist_stats AS (
  SELECT a.id,
         a.name,
         count(*)                  AS track_count,
         round(avg(t.popularity), 1) AS avg_popularity
  FROM artists a
  JOIN track_artists ta ON ta.artist_id = a.id
  JOIN tracks t         ON t.id = ta.track_id
  GROUP BY a.id, a.name
)
SELECT name, track_count, avg_popularity
FROM artist_stats
WHERE track_count >= 20
ORDER BY avg_popularity DESC
LIMIT 25;

queries.title: Correlated subquery: each artist's best track
queries.sql:
SELECT a.name AS artist,
       (SELECT t.name
          FROM tracks t
          JOIN track_artists ta ON ta.track_id = t.id
         WHERE ta.artist_id = a.id
         ORDER BY t.popularity DESC
         LIMIT 1) AS best_track,
       a.followers
FROM artists a
ORDER BY a.followers DESC
LIMIT 20;

queries.title: Recursive CTE: walking the 'fans also like' graph
queries.sql:
WITH RECURSIVE seed AS (
  -- start from whichever artist has the most outgoing edges
  SELECT artist_id AS id
  FROM artist_related
  GROUP BY artist_id
  ORDER BY count(*) DESC
  LIMIT 1
),
reach AS (
  SELECT id, 0 AS depth FROM seed
  UNION ALL
  SELECT ar.related_artist_id, r.depth + 1
  FROM reach r
  JOIN artist_related ar ON ar.artist_id = r.id
  WHERE r.depth < 2
)
SELECT min(r.depth) AS hops, a.name
FROM reach r
JOIN artists a ON a.id = r.id
GROUP BY a.name
ORDER BY hops, a.name
LIMIT 40;

queries.title: Collaborations: tracks with 3+ credited artists
queries.sql:
SELECT t.name AS track,
       string_agg(a.name, ' + ' ORDER BY ta.position) AS artists,
       t.popularity
FROM tracks t
JOIN track_artists ta ON ta.track_id = t.id
JOIN artists a        ON a.id = ta.artist_id
GROUP BY t.id, t.name, t.popularity
HAVING count(*) >= 3
ORDER BY t.popularity DESC
LIMIT 25;

queries.title: LEFT JOIN: tracks whose artist we never got
queries.sql:
-- The source dataset references some artist ids that are missing from
-- artists.csv, so those links were dropped. An INNER JOIN hides these
-- tracks entirely; a LEFT JOIN finds them.
SELECT t.name, t.release_date, t.popularity
FROM tracks t
LEFT JOIN track_artists ta ON ta.track_id = t.id
WHERE ta.track_id IS NULL
ORDER BY t.popularity DESC
LIMIT 20;

queries.title: UNION ALL: the extremes in one result
queries.sql:
(SELECT 'loudest'  AS bucket, name, round(loudness::numeric, 2) AS loudness
   FROM tracks ORDER BY loudness DESC LIMIT 5)
UNION ALL
(SELECT 'quietest' AS bucket, name, round(loudness::numeric, 2)
   FROM tracks ORDER BY loudness ASC  LIMIT 5)
ORDER BY loudness DESC;

queries.title: Unnesting the genres array
queries.sql:
SELECT g              AS genre,
       count(*)       AS artists,
       round(avg(a.popularity), 1) AS avg_popularity,
       sum(a.followers)            AS total_followers
FROM artists a
CROSS JOIN LATERAL unnest(a.genres) AS g
GROUP BY g
ORDER BY artists DESC
LIMIT 25;

queries.title: A transaction you can safely roll back
Reading an execution plan
queries.sql:
EXPLAIN ANALYZE
SELECT a.name, count(*) AS tracks
FROM artists a
JOIN track_artists ta ON ta.artist_id = a.id
GROUP BY a.name
ORDER BY tracks DESC
LIMIT 10;

queries.title: CREATE TABLE ... AS, then inspect
ALTER TABLE and a computed backfill
UPSERT with ON CONFLICT
A view that hides the join
queries.sql:
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW v_tracks_with_artists AS
SELECT t.id,
       t.name       AS track,
       t.popularity,
       t.release_date,
       string_agg(a.name, ', ' ORDER BY ta.position) AS artists
FROM tracks t
JOIN track_artists ta ON ta.track_id = t.id
JOIN artists a        ON a.id = ta.artist_id
GROUP BY t.id, t.name, t.popularity, t.release_date;

SELECT track, artists, popularity
FROM v_tracks_with_artists
ORDER BY popularity DESC
LIMIT 20;

queries.title: Materialized view + REFRESH
A function with a body
queries.sql:
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION decade_of(d date)
RETURNS int
LANGUAGE sql
IMMUTABLE
AS $$
  SELECT (EXTRACT(YEAR FROM d)::int / 10) * 10;
$$;

SELECT decade_of(release_date) AS decade, count(*) AS tracks
FROM tracks
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1;
